context.requirement_text: Fourth requirement of S7. Ports and runs, via REQ-205's harness, the three Meridian scenario YAMLs confirmed present in R-Co: meridian-loan-origination-above-threshold.yaml (large-loan committee quorum), meridian-loan-origination-below-threshold.yaml (small-loan standard authority, EO-002 negative assertion on committee-vote task absence), and meridian-regulatory-compliance-review-bafin.yaml (21-day SLA regulatory escalation, step 3 blocked on the already-filed ISS-0389 advance-timer gap). See docs/requirements.yaml REQ-208 entry for full acceptance criteria.
context.design_doc_summary: Design PASSed CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR at recheck1 (OQ-1 resolved via Instances.get_by_id/2's current_nodes field). Key design elements: (1) new :no_task_of_type Runner verification method for EO-002's negative assertion, querying Tasks.list_tasks/2 across all statuses; (2) new :blocked step disposition (distinct from :skip) with fixed :blocker severity and required blocked_by field; (3) 3 Meridian scenario YAMLs using the real process_claim_intake.yaml/process_policy_binding.yaml fixtures via test-local simplified graphs (SERVICE_TASK elision, REQ-206/207 precedent); (4) BaFin step 3 :blocked citing ISS-0389 (not duplicated); (5) report must state REQ-199's status at execution time plus the sequential-dispatch caveat (design §0.5).

task.description: Implement REQ-208 per the approved design (lib/letflow/design/req208-meridian-scenario-execution.md). Extend test/support/simulation/runner.ex and scenario_fixture.ex additively with :no_task_of_type and :blocked; author the 3 Meridian scenario YAMLs under test/fixtures/simulation/meridian/scenarios/; write test/letflow/simulation/req208_meridian_test.exs; run all 3 scenarios for real against a real running instance; run mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix letflow.check.test; report findings via result.issues.
acceptance_criteria: meridian-loan-origination-above-threshold runs end to end: all three parallel assessment tracks are confirmed created from real queried task state, the committee-vote route is confirmed taken (not the L1/L2 chain) once the eligibility gate clears, quorum 2-of-3 is confirmed reached from the actual committee_outcome variable, and disbursement completes on end-disbursed

meridian-loan-origination-below-threshold runs end to end and EO-002's negative assertion (no committee-vote task exists for any actor) is verified by querying real task state and confirming absence, not merely by the L1/L2 tasks being present

meridian-regulatory-compliance-review-bafin's steps 1 and 2 run for real against real queried state; step 3 is recorded BLOCKED (not SKIP) citing REQ-206's already-filed advance-timer finding rather than filing a duplicate, and the report states explicitly that this same missing capability now blocks scenarios in two different tenant batches

the requirement's report states explicitly whether REQ-199 (correlated effect ordering) was status: done at the time this requirement executed, and if it was still in_progress or blocked, states that as a material caveat on the parallel-track and quorum assertions above rather than silently proceeding as if the dependency were closed
the requirement's report states a closed disposition for every one of the three scenarios -- no step or scenario left unaddressed
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted

result.summary: REQ-208 implemented, but AC1/AC2 could NOT be fully verified as originally designed -- a genuine, pre-existing Engine defect discovered this session (join_counters: %{} hardcoded on every Engine.complete_task/3 call, lib/letflow/engine.ex build_instance_state/3) means a PARALLEL_GATEWAY join can only fire within the SAME hop-chain as its own split; any real, separate-call HUMAN_TASK completion on a fork branch fails with a real HTTP 500. Both loan-origination scenarios were truncated (their own YAML header comments disclose this) to the steps that DO run for real: instance creation (forks 3 real parallel tracks), the first branch's task lookup, and the first branch's task completion, which reproduces the defect (asserted explicitly as the real, closed disposition for that step -- not fabricated as :ok). AC1/AC2's fuller claims (committee route, quorum, disbursement, EO-002's negative assertion) are NOT verified by this run; stated explicitly in test/reports/req208-meridian-scenario-findings.yaml rather than silently assumed to hold. meridian-regulatory-compliance-review-bafin is unaffected (no PARALLEL_GATEWAY on its exercised path) and runs exactly as designed: steps 1/2 real, step 3 :blocked citing ISS-0389. Runner/ScenarioFixture extended additively with :no_task_of_type and :blocked (used by the BaFin scenario and structurally present for the loan scenarios' original EO-002 design, though not reachable in this run). mix compile --warnings-as-errors: clean. mix format --check-formatted: clean. mix letflow.check.test (full suite): exit 1, 3 pre-existing failures unrelated to REQ-208's own change set -- 2 rust-pin toolchain tests fail because this sandbox has no `rustc` on PATH at all (environment fact, not a code regression) and 1 Lua-executor timing-comparison test is flaky under full-suite system load (re-run alone: 48/48 passed). All 3 independently re-run in isolation and reproduced identically, confirming they are not caused by this run's own diff (test/support/simulation/*, test/fixtures/simulation/meridian/*, test/letflow/simulation/req208_meridian_test.exs touch none of the affected files) -- same disposition ISS-0068 already established for this class of finding. test/letflow/simulation/: 28/28 passed (REQ-205/206/207/208 combined).

AC1.evidence: meridian-loan-origination-above-threshold runs for real through step 1 (instance creation, real 3-way parallel fork -- credit-memo-review and risk-assessment both real PENDING HUMAN_TASKs, confirmed via step 2a's own captured GET /tasks response and a direct Tasks.list_tasks/2 query) and step 2a (real task lookup). Step 2b (the first branch's real task completion) returns a real HTTP 500, reproducing the join_counters-not-persisted-across-calls defect (see result.issues) -- this is the scenario's genuine, closed disposition for that step, not a fabricated pass. The committee route, quorum 2-of-3, and disbursement-on-end-disbursed claims are NOT reachable and are NOT verified by this run. Real-state evidence confirms the failed call left no partial corruption (credit-memo-review task still PENDING, instance still ACTIVE at the same 2 nodes).

AC2.evidence: meridian-loan-origination-below-threshold reproduces the identical defect at the identical point (its graph is identical to the above-threshold scenario up to step 2b). EO-002's own literal negative assertion (no committee-vote task exists) cannot be verified via the intended full end-to-end run, since the run cannot progress past the first parallel-branch completion -- stated explicitly in the report, not silently assumed to still hold.

AC3.evidence: meridian-regulatory-compliance-review-bafin unaffected by the PARALLEL_GATEWAY defect (no parallel gateway on its exercised path). Steps 1/2 (create + evidence-collection lookup/complete) run for real against real queried state (step 2a's own captured response confirms evidence-collection existed; a live post-run query confirms current_nodes == ["risk-evaluation"] and a real PENDING risk-evaluation task assigned to role-risk-manager). Step 3/4 (design's step 3, this scenario's own 4th real+blocked entry) is :blocked, blocked_by "ISS-0389", severity :blocker -- citing the already-filed finding, not duplicating it. Report states the cross-tenant finding (same gap now blocks SwiftRoute/REQ-206 and Meridian/REQ-208).

AC4.evidence: docs/requirements.yaml REQ-199 entry re-confirmed status: done, stage S6, this session. Material caveat stated in test/reports/req208-meridian-scenario-findings.yaml's req_199_caveat field: the parallel-fork/join shape's own sequential-dispatch limitation (design §0.5) is now MOOT for a stronger reason than anticipated -- the critical_finding (join_counters never persisted across calls) means no scenario in this codebase can currently drive a PARALLEL_GATEWAY join to fire across two separate task-completion calls at all, not merely that concurrent completions are unproven.

AC5.evidence: test/reports/req208-meridian-scenario-findings.yaml states a closed disposition for every one of the 3 scenarios and every one of their steps: above-threshold (3/3 steps real, closed outcomes :ok/:ok/:error), below-threshold (3/3 steps real, closed outcomes :ok/:ok/:error), BaFin (4 steps: 3 real :ok + 1 :blocked). No step or scenario left unaddressed -- the truncation of the two loan scenarios from their originally-designed step counts is itself disclosed, not silent.

AC6.evidence: mix compile --warnings-as-errors: clean, exit 0 (quoted in check_test_output/compile_output above). mix letflow.check.test (full 2997-test + 6-property suite): exit 1, 3 failures -- ALL 3 independently reproduced in isolation and confirmed pre-existing/environmental, unrelated to REQ-208's own change set (2 rust-pin tests fail solely because this sandbox has no rustc binary; 1 Lua-executor timing test is flaky under full-suite load, passes 48/48 alone). This run's own new/changed code passes clean: mix test test/letflow/simulation/req208_meridian_test.exs -- 3/3 passed; mix test test/letflow/simulation/ (all REQ-205/206/207/208 simulation tests combined) -- 28/28 passed. Reported honestly as PARTIAL rather than PASS since the literal full-suite exit code is nonzero -- REVIEWER/RELEASE-VALIDATOR should independently confirm the pre-existing-failure disposition rather than trust this claim on its own, per this project's own redundancy principle.

issues.title: Engine.complete_task/3's freshly-rebuilt InstanceState always has join_counters: %{} -- a PARALLEL_GATEWAY join can never fire across two separate calls, blocking every scenario whose fork branches require separate HUMAN_TASK completions
issues.description: Discovered this session while implementing REQ-208's committee-quorum/parallel-fork-join scenarios. lib/letflow/engine.ex's build_instance_state/3 (used by Engine.complete_task/3's real, per-call state-rebuild -- confirmed by reading build_snapshot_and_state/4, ~line 1721, and build_instance_state/3, ~line 1813) hardcodes join_counters: %{} on every call, per that function's own code comment: "join_counters is always %{} (design doc §6.5, §11 INV-EE48-7, MAJOR OQ-3): no table persists JoinCounter state across calls today." Independently reproduced this session: Engine.create/2 correctly forks a 3-branch PARALLEL_GATEWAY split within its own single hop-chain (2 real HUMAN_TASKs created, credit-memo-review/risk-assessment), but the very next, separate Engine.complete_task/3 call completing one branch fails with {:error, {:activation_failed, {:unknown_branch_id, _}}} the instant its hop-chain tries to route through the join -- Transition.dispatch_parallel_join/4's own `with %JoinCounter{} <- Map.get(instance_state.join_counters, node.id)` finds nothing, since the freshly-rebuilt seed state's join_counters is always empty. REQ-054 (SnapshotWriter, status: done) DOES serialize join_counters correctly into instance_state_snapshots (lib/letflow/engine/snapshot_writer.ex confirms this) -- but Engine.complete_task/3's own hot path never reads that table at all; it always rebuilds state fresh from tokens/tasks directly. This means EVERY process with a PARALLEL_GATEWAY split whose branches require separate task completions -- not just REQ-208's Meridian scenarios -- cannot actually converge at its join in real, multi-call usage today, despite REQ-051 (parallel gateway split/join) and REQ-048 (task completion) both being status: done and unit-tested at the Transition-module level (test/letflow/engine/parallel_gateway_test.exs exercises Transition.transition/3 directly, in-memory, never through the real per-call state-rebuild path this defect lives in). The gap was flagged as MAJOR OQ-3 in REQ-048's own design doc at the time (lib/letflow/design/req048-task-completion.md §13) and explicitly deferred to "REQ-054 territory" -- but REQ-054 shipped the serialization half only, never wired complete_task/3's hot path to consult it. Not fixable within REQ-208's own scope (this is Engine-core work, its own CODE-DESIGNER-sized task).

issues.title: S7's simulation harness (Letflow.Simulation.Runner) never dispatches steps concurrently -- REQ-199's ORD-01/02/03 guards remain unit-tested (S6) but never exercised end-to-end under real concurrent HTTP load by any S7 scenario
issues.description: Reference/reinforcement of design §7's own recommendation (checked against ISS-0388..0393 first, per the requirement's own instruction -- none of the six cover this; not a duplicate). Runner.run_steps/1 (test/support/simulation/runner.ex) dispatches every via: api step in a strict Enum.reduce, one HTTP call at a time -- there is no mechanism today for two steps to race against the same correlation/instance. This means no S7 scenario, including REQ-208's, provides end-to-end evidence that ORD-01 (claim guard)/ORD-02 (execute guard)/ORD-03 (order guard) hold under genuine concurrent completions -- only that S6's own unit tests do. This run's own finding (see the BLOCKER issue above) makes this MORE acute, not less: since a PARALLEL_GATEWAY join cannot even fire sequentially across separate calls today, there is currently no in-flight multi-branch scenario for ORD-01/02/03 to protect on this path at all, until the BLOCKER above is fixed. A future requirement could extend Runner with an opt-in concurrent step-group (e.g. steps sharing a declared "parallel_group" key dispatched via Task.async_stream/3) specifically to close this gap once the join defect is fixed.

Filed for visibility per core-directives.md's own redundancy principle (a later run/host may have rustc installed and could confirm/close this), not because REQ-208 needs to fix either.
